editorial.headline: The Public-Sector Engine Room of Screen Post-Production
editorial.standfirst: Government-managed screen finishing, preservation and delivery work sits in a field closed to foreign investment nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 59121 covers the government-managed work that happens after a film, video, audiovisual work or television programme has been made. Its practical territory includes editing and cutting; dubbing; titles and film credits; closed captioning; animation and special effects; transfers from film or tape; and conversion into video-streaming formats. It also encompasses film studios and specialist animation studios that develop and process film, reproduce it for cinema distribution, and document film recordings or other moving-image stock footage on a fee basis. This is the finishing, preservation and delivery layer of screen production, administered within a government-managed setting.

The remit extends beyond conventional post-production. It includes government-managed post-production involving sports-media content, as well as censorship of films, videos and television programmes when undertaken by a government-managed business entity or business operator as part of the post-production process. That institutional character is central to the activity’s definition. The record places it across Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales, while consistently locating the underlying work in government management. Scale describes the available business classifications; it does not detach the activity from that public-sector context.

Nationally, foreign investment is closed, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 0%. There is therefore no room for a partial foreign stake within this activity’s national foreign-investment position. The relevant national basis cited in the record is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. For a founder assessing a foreign-investment structure, the conclusion is direct: this is not an activity open to foreign ownership at the national level.

Bali reaches the same operational conclusion for PMA registration: the activity is listed as closed, and a foreigner cannot register it in Bali today. The detail matters, however. At the Large scale, the OSS risk is recorded as Medium-High/High, meaning this activity is not blocked by Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium for Low and Medium-Low risk PMA activities. That does not create an opening. It simply distinguishes the moratorium from the separate Bali status recorded for this activity: closed.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali’s moratorium does not apply here, but that does not turn a closed activity into an opening for foreign investment.
